beats.text: Are we born already knowing things — or does the mind start empty? Locke chose empty.
At birth, he said, the mind is like white paper, void of all characters, without any ideas.
So where does everything you know come from? One source: experience. The senses write on the page.
Every concept, even the loftiest, is built from things you first saw, heard, or felt.
It was a quietly radical idea. If we're shaped by experience, then we can be shaped better.
Change the schooling, the environment, the chances — and you change the human being.
No one is born a servant or a king. We are written into what we become.

attribution: John Locke · An Essay Concerning Human Understanding
source_note: Quote: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1689, public domain).
